text: It’s partly a small sample size thing but I also do firmly believe Brown, as much I loved the Jays era and that championship run, is not as obviously plug and play as people think. It’s not necessarily entirely a skill set thing either, it’s partly his mindset. When he isn’t doing the scoring or on-ball defense he doesn’t actually contribute a ton. He’s a fine 3 ball shooter, but not great, and he’s not good on defense off-ball. His passing and vision is also mediocre. Maxey, as I understand it, also isn’t much of a passer. They may have some issues where the ball sticks too much when they all play together, and I don’t even mean that in an “there’s only so many touches” way, just that their best individual scorers are not their best team playmakers. This would ideally be offset by LeBron being one of the great passers and playmakers in the history of the sport, if not the greatest for the latter, but he’s not the guy he was at 38 let alone 28, so he can’t carry the load and collapse the defense while the others play off-ball. I think they can figure this out (they came into the night 9-2!) but I also think that will require better staggering of minutes to get a couple guys who know how to play as roleplayers on the court more often to offset the fact they don’t really have an exceptional passer among their stars that isn’t pushing 42.
label: hot_take
